checkpoints.label: 1 · Release
checkpoints.narrative: J/K/L/M release 4 lanes at their frontiers while F/G/H/I keep decoding under existing grants.

checkpoints.label: 2 · Plan
checkpoints.narrative: Completion debt assigns 1 to `f_4`, 3 to `f_8` from the 4 released lanes, with no supply miss or spill.

checkpoints.label: 3 · Apply
checkpoints.narrative: Apply O → `f_4`, J → `f_8`, P → `f_8`, Q → `f_8` to the released lanes while preserving the 4 frozen grants and parking unselected requests.

attrs.supporting_note:
`f_2` means two decoded chunks; `f_2 → f_4` grants execution up to four chunks.

`B1/B2/B4/B8` are final-length buckets; unfinished requests have no observed completion bucket.

Debt = target − observed completions; service = positive debt × mean length.
The prior uses lengths 1, 2, 4, 8; largest-remainder rounding sets ideal lane counts.
Preserve frozen grants, then allocate released lanes in frontier order and select eligible requests by waiting order within their engine.

Both views use the same checkpoint: Plan changes no request state, and Apply advances no decode time.
Request fill uses the original rollout teal/amber palette for decoded progress; intermediate values use the last reached frontier. Shade does not imply completion.
Completed and pending requests are summarized; all requests remain in the Python model.
attrs.operation_legend:
**Progress colors:** light teal `f_1` · teal `f_2` · light amber `f_4` · amber `f_8`.

**Orange outline:** current decision; fill follows decoded progress, not the next grant.
